detail.runner_up_case: The claim asserts personal ownership: 'Vijay Mallya was the owner of Kingfisher Airlines.' On a strict reading, 'owner' means holding the equity, and the assembled record does not establish that. The team's own evidence says the airline 'was owned by the Bengaluru based United Breweries Group' — a corporate group, not Mallya personally. The only shareholding record in evidence shows Mallya's personal direct stake in Kingfisher Airlines Ltd at just 1.87%, listed as 'Promoter' alongside group vehicles (UB Overseas Ltd 1.68%, Sashikar Enterprises 1.98%), i.e., the controlling equity sat with UB Group companies of which he was chairman, not with him as an individual. The Reuters citation shows he owned 8.1% of United Breweries, the beer company — not of the airline. Everything else cited (BBC 'chairman', Wikipedia 'CMD', Seven Pillars 'started the airline') establishes a founder/leadership role, not personal legal ownership. So the accurate statement is: Mallya founded, chaired and controlled Kingfisher Airlines as promoter through United Breweries (Holding) Ltd and allied entities; the owner of record was the UB Group. If TRUE requires the assertion as stated to be accurate, 'was the owner' is materially wrong as a statement of personal ownership. Honest caveat: business-press usage routinely calls a controlling promoter the 'owner' (BBC itself uses that shorthand), so many reviewers would grade this MIXED rather than FALSE; the FALSE case rests entirely on the strict legal-ownership reading, and it is weakened by the absence of any source affirmatively denying Mallya control.
would_flip_it: BSE/NSE annual-report shareholding patterns or MCA filings for Kingfisher Airlines Ltd (2003-2012) showing that Vijay Vittal Mallya personally held no shares at any point and held no directorship — i.e., the CMD/promoter attributions are wrong.
Registry or court evidence that the 'Vijay Mallya' named as Kingfisher Airlines CMD/promoter is a different namesake, not Vijay Vittal Mallya (b. 18 December 1955).

An authoritative finding (SEBI, MCA, PMLA adjudication, or a court) that Kingfisher Airlines was owned and controlled by persons or entities other than Mallya, with him holding neither equity nor control.

Incorporation and capitalization records showing Kingfisher Airlines was founded and funded by United Breweries (Holding) Ltd or other shareholders in which Mallya himself held no stake and no board seat — severing both the direct and the indirect-control routes to 'owner'.
